# Cascade docs

> Cascade traces an ML workload once on a real GPU and simulates it on many GPU configs at once with Accel-Sim.


# Introduction

Page: index.html

Cascade takes a trace of an ML workload captured on one real GPU and simulates it on other GPU configs, many copies at once. You trace once, then ask how the same kernels run on an H100, an H200 or a dozen replicas of each.

## How it fits together

Cascade has three parts. Each part runs in a different place, and they talk over S3 and plain HTTP.

Diagram: The profiler uploads to the app's S3 endpoint. The app forks one simulator per GPU config replica. Simulators send heartbeats and logs back to the app.

- **Profiler.** Runs your workload, such as a `vLLM` model, on a Modal H100 under Accel-Sim's NVBit tracer. It uploads each kernel's trace to the Cascade app while tracing is still running.
- **Cascade app.** One Sail sandbox that receives traces over S3, gets them ready to simulate, launches runs, and shows everything in a web UI and an HTTP API.
- **Simulators.** Each simulator is a fork of the app's sandbox, so it starts with the trace already on disk. It runs Accel-Sim against one GPU config and reports progress back to the app.

## What works today

Two things are still in progress, and they change what you see.

- A default deploy runs a stand-in simulator, `cascade worker --replay`, which replays a recorded Accel-Sim log instead of simulating your trace. To simulate your trace, deploy with `--base-image`, `--sim-cmd` and `--accelsim-dir` pointing at an image that has Accel-Sim built in. See [Deploy the app](deploy.html).
- The profiler doesn't capture real hardware timing (`real_timing.json`) yet. Until it does, the real-against-simulated comparison shows simulated time only.

## Where to go next

- [Quickstart](quickstart.html): Run the app on your laptop with the stand-in simulator and finish a run in a few minutes.
- [Concepts](concepts.html): Traces, runs, sims and GPU configs, their state machines, and how forking works.
- [Trace a workload](trace-a-workload.html): Capture a vLLM model on a Modal H100 and stream it into your app.
- [API reference](api.html): Every route, with real responses captured from a running server.
- [Bring your own simulator](simulator.html): The contract a program follows to run as a Cascade simulator.
- [Types](types.html): Every request and response model, generated from `cascade/models.py`.


# Quickstart

Page: quickstart.html

In this quickstart, we run the Cascade app on your laptop, upload a small stand-in trace, simulate it on two copies of the `SM86_RTX3070` config, and download the results.

The simulators here are `cascade worker --replay`, which replays a recorded Accel-Sim log of BabelStream on an RTX 3070 instead of running Accel-Sim. Every number you see comes from that log, not from the trace you upload. The point is to see the whole loop work before you deploy for real.

## Before you start

You need these on your machine.

- `git` and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). uv installs Python 3.12 for you.
- `rclone`, which serves the app's S3 endpoint. On macOS, run `brew install rclone`.
- Node 22, only if you want the web UI. Everything else works without it.

## Run the loop

1. **Clone and install.**

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/atoniolo76/cascade.git
   cd cascade
   uv sync
   ```

   To get the web UI as well, build it once. The build lands in `cascade/static/`, which the app serves.

   ```bash
   (cd web && npm ci && npm run build)
   ```

2. **Start the app.** This runs the API and UI on port 8000 and the S3 endpoint on port 9000. Leave it running and open a second terminal for the next steps.

   ```bash
   export CASCADE_TOKEN=dev-token
   CASCADE_DATA_DIR=./data \
   CASCADE_ACCELSIM_DIR=$PWD/tests/fixtures/accelsim \
   CASCADE_SIM_CMD="$PWD/.venv/bin/cascade worker --replay $PWD/tests/fixtures/logs/babelstream_sm86_rtx3070.log" \
   uv run cascade serve
   ```

   When the app is up, the log ends with this line.

   ```text
   INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
   ```

3. **Make a stand-in trace.** The replaying worker only checks that `traces/kernelslist.g` exists, so one line is enough. A real trace comes from the profiler. See [Trace a workload](trace-a-workload.html).

   ```bash
   export CASCADE_TOKEN=dev-token CASCADE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000
   mkdir -p demo/traces
   echo kernel-1.traceg > demo/traces/kernelslist.g
   ```

4. **Upload it.** `scripts/upload_trace.py` uploads a directory the same way the profiler does and sends `metadata.json` last. The two `--meta` flags tell the app which GPU architecture the trace is for and which config to suggest.

   ```bash
   uv run python scripts/upload_trace.py demo --run-name demo \
     --meta trace_gpu_arch=sm_86 --meta suggested_sim_config=SM86_RTX3070
   ```

   You see each file go up.

   ```text
   uploaded traces/kernelslist.g (16 bytes)
   uploaded metadata.json (1 files listed) to s3://cascade/accelsim-traces/demo/
   ```

5. **Wait for the trace to be ready.** The app scans the bucket every 2 seconds. Because the upload already has `kernelslist.g`, it skips post-processing.

   ```bash
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASCADE_TOKEN" "$CASCADE_URL/api/traces/demo"
   ```

   Repeat until the response has `"state":"ready"`. It takes a few seconds.

6. **Launch a run.** This asks for two sims on `SM86_RTX3070` and saves the run's id.

   ```bash
   RUN=$(curl -s -X POST "$CASCADE_URL/api/runs" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASCADE_TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"trace_id": "demo", "entries": [{"gpu_config": "SM86_RTX3070", "count": 2}]}' \
     | python3 -c 'import json, sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["id"])')
   echo $RUN
   ```

7. **Watch it finish.** Each sim replays about 10,000 log lines and finishes in a few seconds.

   ```bash
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASCADE_TOKEN" "$CASCADE_URL/api/runs/$RUN" \
     | python3 -c 'import json, sys; r = json.load(sys.stdin); print(r["state"], r["sim_counts"])'
   ```

   When both sims are done, you see this.

   ```text
   succeeded {'succeeded': 2}
   ```

   If you built the UI, open [http://127.0.0.1:8000](http://127.0.0.1:8000), paste `dev-token`, and open the run to see the same thing live.

8. **Download the results.** This saves one JSON file with the run, the trace, every sim's per-kernel stats, and the comparison.

   ```bash
   curl -s -OJ -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASCADE_TOKEN" "$CASCADE_URL/api/runs/$RUN/results"
   ```

   The file is named `<run id>-results.json`. [Reading results](reading-results.html) explains what's in it.

To stop, press Ctrl+C in the first terminal. The app stops rclone too. Your traces and runs stay in `./data` for next time.

## Next steps

- [Concepts](concepts.html) explains what a trace, a run and a sim are, and how their states move.
- [Deploy the app](deploy.html) runs the same app on Sail, where each sim is its own sandbox.
- [Bring your own simulator](simulator.html) replaces the replay with Accel-Sim or anything else.


# Use with AI agents

Page: agents.html

Paste one prompt into your agent and it can work your Cascade app for you. It reads your traces, launches runs on the configs that fit, watches them finish, and explains the results.

**Setup prompt**Tells your agent how to authenticate, which routes to call, and how to report results.

## What an agent can do

The agent works through the same [HTTP API](api.html) as the web UI. With the prompt, it can do these things.

- Check traces. It lists them, waits for an upload to become `ready`, and reports a trace that `failed`.
- Launch runs. It picks the GPU configs whose `arch` matches the trace's `trace_gpu_arch` and asks before it starts more than 4 sims.
- Watch runs. It polls the run until every sim has finished and tells you the progress as it goes.
- Pull results and comparisons. It reads per-kernel times from `/kernels`, real against simulated time from `/comparison`, and the full stats from `/results` when you ask for them.
- Explain the numbers. It reports simulated time per config, the error against real hardware when the trace has real timing, the worst kernels by readable name, and why any sim failed.

The agent can't trace a workload. Tracing runs on a real GPU under the Modal profiler, outside the API. [Trace a workload](trace-a-workload.html) covers that part. Once the trace is in your app, the agent takes it from there.

> A default deploy runs the stand-in simulator, which replays one recorded Accel-Sim run of OPT-125m on an H100 for every trace. The prompt tells the agent to say so when the numbers look like the stand-in's, so a report never passes them off as a simulation of your trace.

## Set it up

1. **Put the app's URL and token in the agent's environment.** Run this in the terminal you start the agent from, then start the agent. The prompt tells the agent to read the token from `$CASCADE_TOKEN` and never print it.

   ```bash
   export CASCADE_URL=https://<your-app>
   export CASCADE_TOKEN=<your token>
   ```

   The URL is the one `deploy_sail.py` prints as `app:`. Locally it is `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.

2. **Give the agent the prompt.** Copy the [setup prompt](agents.html#the-setup-prompt) and paste it into the chat, or save it where your agent reads instructions, as [Set up your tool](agents.html#set-up-your-tool) shows.

3. **Ask for what you want.** For example:

   ```text
   Which of my traces are ready?
   Simulate the newest trace on every config that matches it, one sim each, and compare them.
   Why did sims fail in my last run?
   ```

## The setup prompt

The build generates the API, state and type sections of this prompt from `landing/docs-src/endpoints.py` and `cascade/models.py`, the same sources as the [API reference](api.html). It always matches the API these docs describe. If you saved a copy, copy it again after you update Cascade.

agent-prompt.md:

````
# Cascade

You are working with a Cascade app. Cascade takes a trace of a GPU workload, captured once on a real GPU, and simulates it with Accel-Sim on other GPU configs, many sims at once. You drive the app over its HTTP API. You can check traces, launch runs, watch them, pull results and comparisons, and explain the numbers to the user.

You cannot capture a trace. Tracing runs the workload on a real GPU under Cascade's Modal profiler, outside this API. When the user wants a new trace, tell them to run the profiler (the "Trace a workload" page of the Cascade docs) and then wait for the trace to appear in the app.

Words used below:

- A **trace** is one profiler run. Its `id` is the profiler's run name.
- A **GPU config** is one of Accel-Sim's tested configs, such as `SM90_H100`.
- A **run** is one trace plus a list of entries. Each entry names a GPU config and a `count`.
- A **sim** is one simulator working through the trace on one config. Sims of one entry differ only in `replica`, numbered from 0.

## Connect

The app's URL and token come from two environment variables.

- `CASCADE_URL` is the app's base URL with no trailing slash, such as `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.
- `CASCADE_TOKEN` is the bearer token the app was started with.

Check that both are set without printing them:

```bash
test -n "$CASCADE_URL" && test -n "$CASCADE_TOKEN" && echo set
```

If either is unset, ask the user to export both in the terminal they start you from, and to start you again. If the user gives you the URL or the token in the conversation instead, write them once to a file only they can read, and load that file at the start of every command. Variables you export in one command may be gone in the next. Writing the file is the one command that holds the token's value. When you finish the task, delete it with `rm ~/.cascade.env` and tell the user, unless they ask you to keep it.

```bash
(umask 077 && printf 'export CASCADE_URL=%s CASCADE_TOKEN=%s\n' '<url>' '<token>' > ~/.cascade.env)
. ~/.cascade.env && curl -sS --fail-with-body -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASCADE_TOKEN" "$CASCADE_URL/api/traces"
```

Send the token on every request as an `Authorization: Bearer` header. Write every request in this form, with the variables unexpanded, so the token never appears in a command or its output:

```bash
curl -sS --fail-with-body -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASCADE_TOKEN" "$CASCADE_URL/api/traces"
```

For a request with a JSON body, add `-X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '<json>'`. When the status is 400 or more, `--fail-with-body` makes curl exit with code 22, print `The requested URL returned error: <status>` and still print the JSON body. Parse responses with `jq` or `python3`, and aggregate large responses in the command instead of printing them whole.

Check the connection before anything else.

1. `GET /api/health` needs no token. Expect `{"ok": true, "auth": true}`. Anything else means `CASCADE_URL` is wrong or the app is down. `"auth": false` means the app runs without a token check, which is fine.
2. `GET /api/traces` with the token. A `401` means the token is wrong. Stop and ask the user to check `CASCADE_TOKEN`.

The connection is good when both calls succeed.

## Procedure

Follow these steps to simulate a trace and report on it. When the user asks about an existing run, start at step 5 with its `id`. `GET /api/runs` lists runs newest first.

1. **Find the trace.** Call `GET /api/traces`. Keep the traces whose `state` is `ready`. Match the user's words against `id`, `model`, `layers` and `source_gpu`. If more than one trace matches, list each with its `id`, `model`, `layers`, `trace_gpu_arch`, `kernel_count` and `created_at`, and ask which one. If the trace the user means is `uploading` or `processing`, poll `GET /api/traces/{trace_id}` every 10 seconds until it is `ready`. If it is `failed`, report its `error` and stop. This step is done when you hold one `ready` trace and its `trace_gpu_arch`.
2. **Pick the configs.** Call `GET /api/gpu-configs`. Keep only the configs whose `arch` equals the trace's `trace_gpu_arch`. A trace can only run on configs of its own architecture. Use the configs the user named. If they named none, use the trace's `suggested_sim_config` when it is set, and otherwise every matching config. If a config the user named has another `arch`, say so and offer the matching ones. This step is done when every config you will use has the trace's `arch`.
3. **Size the run.** Each entry's `count`, from 1 to 64, is how many replicas run that config. Use 1 per config unless the user asks for more. Suggest 3 when the user wants to know whether the numbers are stable. Add up the counts. If the total is more than 4 sims, show the user the entries and the total and wait for them to agree. On Sail, every sim is its own forked sandbox, and each one costs money. This step is done when you have the entries and, above 4 sims, the user's yes.
4. **Launch the run.** Call `POST /api/runs` with `{"trace_id": "<trace id>", "entries": [{"gpu_config": "<name>", "count": 1}]}`. A `201` returns the run. Save its `id`. Launch once. If the call fails with a network error or a `5xx`, call `GET /api/runs` and look for a new run on this trace before you try again.
5. **Watch the run.** Poll `GET /api/runs/{run_id}` every 10 seconds until `state` is anything but `active`. Between polls, tell the user the counts in `sim_counts` and each sim's `kernels_done` out of `kernels_total`. If `kernels_done` passes `kernels_total`, give both numbers as they are, cap any percentage at 100, and treat it as a stand-in sign (see Rules). A `lost` sim can come back, so keep waiting. A sim that stays `lost` for 10 times the heartbeat timeout, 600 seconds by default, becomes `failed`. A real Accel-Sim run can take hours. If the run is still `active` after about 5 minutes, give the user the run `id` and the progress, and offer to check again later. `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/events` streams the same changes as server-sent events, but the stream never closes, so polling is simpler. To read the stream anyway, add `-N --max-time 30` to curl. This step is done when the run's `state` is `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
6. **Fetch the results.** Call `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/kernels` for every sim's per-kernel times and `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/comparison` for real against simulated time per kernel. A `KernelStat` names only its `sim_id`. Join it to the run's `sims` by `id` to get its `gpu_config`, `replica` and `state`. For each sim that did not succeed, read `error`, `exit_code` and `log_tail` from the run. If `log_tail` does not explain the failure, read the end of `GET /api/sims/{sim_id}/log`, then search the whole log with `grep -inE 'error|abort|assert|fault|exception'`. If nothing explains it, report that the log does not show a cause, and give the `exit_code`, the signal it implies (134 is SIGABRT, 137 is SIGKILL, 139 is SIGSEGV), and the last kernel the sim reached. Call `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/results` only when the user asks for the full Accel-Sim stats. It carries about 30 KB per kernel. This step is done when you hold the kernels, the comparison and the reason for every sim that did not succeed.
7. **Report.** Write the report as the next section describes.

## Report

Lead with one line that gives the run `id`, the trace `id`, the run `state`, and the sim counts. Then cover these points, in this order.

1. **Simulated time per config.** For each sim, add up `sim_time_ns` over its kernels from `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/kernels`. For each config, give the median of those totals over the replicas that succeeded, and the lowest and highest total when there is more than one replica. A sim that did not succeed has only the kernels it finished, so leave it out of the totals. If no replica of a config succeeded, say so. Name the fastest config and give every other config as a multiple of it. When configs are within 1% of each other, say they tie instead of naming a winner. When the numbers come from the stand-in, say the configs cannot be compared from this run. Also give `latest.gpu_tot_sim_cycle` and `latest.gpu_tot_ipc` per config, from the run's sims. This computes the totals:

```bash
curl -sS --fail-with-body -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASCADE_TOKEN" "$CASCADE_URL/api/runs/<run id>" > /tmp/cascade-run.json
curl -sS --fail-with-body -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASCADE_TOKEN" "$CASCADE_URL/api/runs/<run id>/kernels" > /tmp/cascade-kernels.json
python3 -c '
import json, statistics
run = json.load(open("/tmp/cascade-run.json"))
sims = {s["id"]: s for s in run["sims"]}
totals = {}
for k in json.load(open("/tmp/cascade-kernels.json")):
    totals[k["sim_id"]] = totals.get(k["sim_id"], 0) + (k["sim_time_ns"] or 0)
configs = {}
for sim, total in totals.items():
    if sims[sim]["state"] == "succeeded":
        configs.setdefault(sims[sim]["gpu_config"], []).append(total)
for name, values in sorted(configs.items()):
    print(name, "median", statistics.median(values), "lowest", min(values), "highest", max(values), "replicas", len(values))
'
```
2. **Accuracy against real hardware.** When the comparison has `has_real_timing` true, compute the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) for each config. Use the rows where both `real_ns` and `sim_ns` for that config are set. MAPE is the mean of `abs(sim_ns - real_ns) / real_ns * 100`. Say how many rows went into it. A row's `sim_ns` is the median over every replica that finished that kernel, including replicas that failed later. When `has_real_timing` is false, say that the trace has no real timing yet, so the report covers simulated time only.
3. **Worst kernels.** Name up to 5 kernels. With real timing, pick those with the largest absolute percentage error. Without it, pick those with the largest share of simulated time, and say how much their time differs between configs. Name each kernel in readable form. Demangle `kernel_name` with `c++filt -n -p <kernel_name>` when `c++filt` is installed, so `_Z11copy_kernelIdEvPKT_PS0_` becomes `copy_kernel<double>`. The `-n` matters on macOS, where `c++filt` without it returns the name unchanged. Without `c++filt`, give the identifier inside the mangled name, such as `copy_kernel`. Give the `kernel_index` too.
4. **Failed, lost and cancelled sims.** List every sim whose `state` is not `succeeded`, with its `id`, `gpu_config`, `replica`, `state`, `error`, `exit_code` and the lines of `log_tail` that show the cause.

When the user wants the simulator's own files, list them with `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/files`, download one with `GET /api/sims/{sim_id}/files/{name}`, and fetch a Perfetto trace of the run with `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/perfetto`.

Give times in the largest unit that keeps the number above 1, such as 5.2 µs or 3.1 ms, and call them simulated. Take every number from an API response. When a value is `null`, say that it is missing. If the user asks what a number means, explain it from the field descriptions under "Types" below.

## Rules

- Keep the token secret. Refer to it only as `$CASCADE_TOKEN`, and never print, echo or repeat its value.
- Launch a run only when the user asked for one. Above 4 sims in total, get the user's yes to the entries first.
- Cancel a run only when the user asks. `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/cancel` stops every sim that has not finished. It is safe to repeat.
- Use `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/kernels` for per-kernel numbers. Use `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/results` only for the full stats maps.
- Check whether the numbers come from Cascade's stand-in simulator, unless the user has said the app runs a real Accel-Sim image. A default deploy runs the stand-in, `cascade worker --replay`, which replays one recorded Accel-Sim run of `facebook/opt-125m` on SM90_H100 (20 vLLM kernels), whatever the trace. A local dev server may replay a BabelStream log instead, whose kernels are named init, copy, mul, add, triad and dot. The signs are the same kernels for every trace (`nvjet_sm90_hsh_64x8_64x16_4x1_v_bz_bias_TNT`, `vllm::reshape_and_cache_flash_kernel`, `cutlass::device_kernel` and `at::native::vectorized_elementwise_kernel` on a default deploy), OPT-125m kernels for a trace of another model, and `kernels_done` different from `kernels_total`. When you see these signs, say at the top of the report that the numbers come from the stand-in and do not describe the trace.
- Never call `POST /api/sims/{sim_id}/heartbeat`, `POST /api/sims/{sim_id}/logs`, `POST /api/sims/{sim_id}/step-timeline` or `PUT /api/sims/{sim_id}/files/{name}`. Those routes are for simulators, and a heartbeat changes a sim's state.
- Lists come back whole, with no pagination.

## Errors

Every error is JSON with a `detail` field.

- **401.** The token is missing or wrong. Stop and ask the user to check `CASCADE_TOKEN`. Do not try other tokens.
- **404.** When `detail` names a trace, run or sim, that id does not exist. List again with `GET /api/traces` or `GET /api/runs` to find the right one. When `detail` is just `Not Found`, the path itself is wrong. Check it against the routes below.
- **409.** `POST /api/runs` named a trace that is not `ready`. `detail` gives its state. If the state is `uploading` or `processing`, wait until the trace is `ready` and launch again. If it is `failed`, report the trace's `error`.
- **422.** When `detail` is a sentence, a `gpu_config` is unknown or has an `arch` other than the trace's `trace_gpu_arch`. Call `GET /api/gpu-configs` and use matching configs. When `detail` is a list, the body is invalid: `entries` is empty, or a `count` is outside 1 to 64. Each item's `loc` and `msg` say what to fix.
- **5xx or a network error.** Retry a `GET` up to 3 times, a few seconds apart. Before you retry `POST /api/runs`, check `GET /api/runs` for the run, so you never launch it twice.

## API

Every route takes the bearer token except `GET /api/health`. Bodies are JSON, and timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.

| method | path | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/health` | Liveness check. Needs no token. |
| GET | `/api/traces` | Every trace, newest first. |
| GET | `/api/traces/{trace_id}` | One trace with its metadata and kernels. |
| GET | `/api/gpu-configs` | The GPU configs a run can use. |
| POST | `/api/runs` | Launch sims for a ready trace. |
| GET | `/api/runs` | Every run, newest first. |
| GET | `/api/runs/{run_id}` | One run with its trace and every sim. |
| POST | `/api/runs/{run_id}/cancel` | Cancel every unfinished sim. |
| GET | `/api/runs/{run_id}/comparison` | Per-kernel real time against simulated time per config. |
| GET | `/api/runs/{run_id}/kernels` | Every sim's per-kernel stats, without the full stats maps. |
| GET | `/api/runs/{run_id}/step-timelines` | Each sim's predicted step timeline and its comparison with the real run. |
| GET | `/api/runs/{run_id}/results` | One JSON file with the run, trace, every sim's stats and the comparison. |
| GET | `/api/sims/{sim_id}/results` | One sim's config, per-kernel stats and totals. |
| GET | `/api/sims/{sim_id}/log` | The sim's full raw output. |
| GET | `/api/runs/{run_id}/files` | Every output file the run's sims uploaded. |
| GET | `/api/runs/{run_id}/perfetto` | The run's simulated kernels as a Chrome trace JSON for ui.perfetto.dev. |
| GET | `/api/sims/{sim_id}/files` | The output files one sim uploaded. |
| GET | `/api/sims/{sim_id}/files/{name}` | One output file, as the sim uploaded it. |
| GET | `/api/runs/{run_id}/events` | Server-sent events for one run. |

### GET /api/health

Check health. Returns `{"ok": true, "auth": true}` while the app process is serving requests. `auth` is `false` only when the app runs with `CASCADE_NO_AUTH=1`, a local-dev mode where no token is needed and the web UI skips its token screen. Health does not check the database, the S3 endpoint or the launcher.

- Auth: No token needed.
- Returns: `200` with `{"ok": true, "auth": true}`.

### GET /api/traces

List traces. Lists every trace the app has registered, in every state, newest first by `created_at`. A trace appears as soon as its first file lands in the bucket, so this list also shows uploads in progress.

- Returns: `200` with a list of `TraceSummary`.

### GET /api/traces/{trace_id}

Get a trace. Returns one trace with the parsed `metadata.json` and every kernel launch read from the trace's `stats_ctx_*` files. `kernels` stays empty until the trace is `ready`.

- Path parameter `trace_id` (str): The trace's `id`, which is the profiler's run name.
- Returns: `200` with a `TraceDetail`.
- `404`: No trace has this id.

### GET /api/gpu-configs

List GPU configs. Lists the GPU configs the app found at startup under `$CASCADE_ACCELSIM_DIR/gpu-simulator/gpgpu-sim/configs/tested-cfgs/*/gpgpusim.config`. The app derives `arch` from the directory name (`SM90_H100` is `sm_90`, `SM7_QV100` is `sm_70`) and reads `core_clock_mhz` from the first value of `-gpgpu_clock_domains`. A directory whose name or clock it can't read is skipped.

- Returns: `200` with a list of `GpuConfig`, sorted by name.

### POST /api/runs

Create a run. Creates a run and starts launching its sims in the background. Each entry fans out to `count` sims, numbered by `replica` from 0. The response comes back before any sim has launched, so every sim is `pending` or `launching`. Follow progress with `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/events` or by polling `GET /api/runs/{run_id}`.

- Body: `RunCreate`.
- Returns: `201` with a `RunDetail`.
- `404`: `trace_id` names no trace.
- `409`: The trace is not `ready`.
- `422`: An entry names an unknown `gpu_config`, or a config whose `arch` differs from the trace's `trace_gpu_arch`.
- `422`: The body fails validation: `entries` is empty, or a `count` is outside 1 to 64.

### GET /api/runs

List runs. Lists every run, newest first, with per-state sim counts. Use `GET /api/runs/{run_id}` for the sims themselves.

- Returns: `200` with a list of `RunSummary`.

### GET /api/runs/{run_id}

Get a run. Returns the run, its trace, and every sim with its state, progress, latest metrics and last 20 log lines.

- Path parameter `run_id` (str): The run's `id`, such as `run-9f56e171af08`.
- Returns: `200` with a `RunDetail`.
- `404`: No run has this id.

### POST /api/runs/{run_id}/cancel

Cancel a run. Moves every sim that has not finished to `cancelled` and asks the launcher to stop it. Sims that already finished keep their state. The next heartbeat from a cancelled sim gets `cancel: true`. Calling it again changes nothing, so it is safe to retry.

- Path parameter `run_id` (str): The run's `id`, such as `run-9f56e171af08`.
- Returns: `200` with the `RunDetail` after cancelling.
- `404`: No run has this id.

### GET /api/runs/{run_id}/comparison

Compare real and simulated time. Lines up kernels by order. Row `i` holds the `i`th kernel the sims finished and the `i`th row of the trace's real timing, sorted by `kernel_id`. For each config, `sim_ns` is the median `sim_time_ns` over that config's replicas, or `null` if no replica has finished that kernel. `real_ns` is `null` until the trace has real timing, which the profiler does not capture yet.

- Path parameter `run_id` (str): The run's `id`, such as `run-9f56e171af08`.
- Returns: `200` with a `Comparison`.
- `404`: No run has this id.

### GET /api/runs/{run_id}/kernels

List a run's kernel timings. Returns a `KernelStat` for every kernel every sim in the run has finished, ordered by config, replica, then kernel. Each `stats` map is empty to keep the response small; the full maps are in the results downloads. Laying each sim's kernels end to end by `sim_time_ns` gives its timeline, which is what the app's timeline and Compare views draw.

- Path parameter `run_id` (str): The run's `id`, such as `run-9f56e171af08`.
- Returns: `200` with a list of `KernelStat`.
- `404`: No run has this id.

### GET /api/runs/{run_id}/step-timelines

List a run's step timing. Returns a `SimStepTimeline` for every sim in the run that has sent step timing, ordered by config, then replica. A sim sends one after it succeeds on a trace whose `has_step_timeline` is true, so the list is empty until then, and stays empty for other traces. `simulated` is a full `simulated_timeline.json`, with every kernel of every step, so for a real model it can be several megabytes per sim. Per-kind step means are in `simulated.summary.per_kind`, coverage is in `simulated.summary.simulation.coverage`, and per-step and per-request errors against the real run are in `compare`.

- Path parameter `run_id` (str): The run's `id`, such as `run-9f56e171af08`.
- Returns: `200` with a list of `SimStepTimeline`.
- `404`: No run has this id.

### GET /api/runs/{run_id}/results

Download run results. Returns everything about a run as one JSON download, with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<run_id>-results.json"`. Each sim's `kernels` carry the full `stats` map, every `key = value` line Accel-Sim printed for that kernel, which is about 30 KB per kernel.

- Path parameter `run_id` (str): The run's `id`, such as `run-9f56e171af08`.
- Returns: `200` with a `RunResults`.
- `404`: No run has this id.

### GET /api/sims/{sim_id}/results

Download sim results. Returns one sim's results as a JSON download named `<sim_id>-results.json`. `totals` is the sim's latest `SimMetrics`.

- Path parameter `sim_id` (str): The sim's `id`, such as `sim-6b4c91e71437`. Find it in `RunDetail.sims`.
- Returns: `200` with a `SimResults`.
- `404`: No sim has this id.

### GET /api/sims/{sim_id}/log

Download a sim's log. Streams every line the simulator sent, in `seq` order, as `text/plain` named `<sim_id>.log`.

- Path parameter `sim_id` (str): The sim's `id`, such as `sim-6b4c91e71437`. Find it in `RunDetail.sims`.
- Returns: `200` with the log as plain text.
- `404`: No sim has this id.

### GET /api/runs/{run_id}/files

List a run's output files. Lists the files every sim in the run uploaded, ordered by config, replica, then name. Each `RunFile` names its sim, so one call covers the run. `cascade worker` uploads a sim's files just before its final heartbeat, so the list grows as sims finish. Fetch one with `GET /api/sims/{sim_id}/files/{name}`.

- Path parameter `run_id` (str): The run's `id`, such as `run-9f56e171af08`.
- Returns: `200` with a list of `RunFile`.
- `404`: No run has this id.

### GET /api/runs/{run_id}/perfetto

Download a Perfetto trace. Builds a Chrome trace JSON from the run's parsed kernel stats and returns it with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<run_id>-perfetto.json"`. Each config is a process, each replica is a thread in it, and each finished kernel is one slice. The app builds it from the stats it parsed, so every run has one, whether or not the simulator wrote its own. Reading results describes the layout.

- Path parameter `run_id` (str): The run's `id`, such as `run-9f56e171af08`.
- Returns: `200` with a Chrome trace JSON object: `traceEvents`, `displayTimeUnit` and `otherData`.
- `404`: No run has this id.

### GET /api/sims/{sim_id}/files

List a sim's output files. Lists one sim's uploaded files, sorted by name. The list is empty until the simulator uploads something.

- Path parameter `sim_id` (str): The sim's `id`, such as `sim-6b4c91e71437`. Find it in `RunDetail.sims`.
- Returns: `200` with a list of `SimFile`.
- `404`: No sim has this id.

### GET /api/sims/{sim_id}/files/{name}

Download an output file. Returns the file as a download named `name`, with the file's `content_type`. A `.gz` file comes back as `application/gzip` with no `Content-Encoding`, so it stays compressed.

- Path parameter `sim_id` (str): The sim's `id`, such as `sim-6b4c91e71437`. Find it in `RunDetail.sims`.
- Path parameter `name` (str): The file's name, such as `kernel-stats.csv`. Letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, 1 to 128 characters, and not `.` or `..`.
- Returns: `200` with the file's bytes.
- `404`: No sim has this id, or the sim has no file with this name.

### GET /api/runs/{run_id}/events

Stream run events. Opens a `text/event-stream`. The first event is always a `snapshot`. After that the stream sends `sim`, `log` and `kernel` events as they happen, and a `: keepalive` comment after 15 seconds without one. The stream does not close when the run finishes.

- Auth: Bearer token, or the token as the `token` query parameter.
- Path parameter `run_id` (str): The run's `id`, such as `run-9f56e171af08`.
- Query parameter `token` (str, optional): Your `CASCADE_TOKEN`. Use it when you can't set headers, as with `EventSource`. If present, it is checked instead of the header.
- Returns: `200` with a `text/event-stream` of `RunEvent`, one JSON object per `data:` line.
- `404`: No run has this id.

## States

### Trace states

A trace's `state`. Runs can only launch on a `ready` trace.

- `uploading`: Files are arriving. `kernel_count` and `bytes` grow on each scan, every 2 seconds. Next: `processing` or `failed`.
- `processing`: The upload is complete. The app is running the trace post-processor, unless the upload already has `traces/kernelslist.g`. Next: `ready` or `failed`.
- `ready`: Post-processing produced `traces/kernelslist.g`. Runs can launch. Terminal.
- `failed`: `metadata.json` has `status: "failed"`, or post-processing failed. `error` says which. Terminal.

### Sim states

A sim's `state`. The app ignores any move not listed here.

- `pending`: Created with the run. Waiting for the launcher. Next: `launching`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
- `launching`: The launcher is starting the sim's sandbox or process. Next: `running`, `lost`, `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
- `running`: The sim sent a `running` heartbeat. Next: `lost`, `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
- `lost`: No heartbeat for `CASCADE_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_S`. A later heartbeat brings it back. Next: `running`, `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
- `succeeded`: The sim sent a `succeeded` heartbeat. Terminal.
- `failed`: The sim sent a `failed` heartbeat, the launcher failed, or it stayed `lost` for 10 times the timeout. Terminal.
- `cancelled`: The run was cancelled before this sim finished. Terminal.

### Run states

`RunState` is not stored. `run_state()` in `cascade/models.py` derives it from the run's sim states each time a run is read.

- `active`: At least one sim has not finished.
- `succeeded`: Every sim succeeded.
- `partial`: Every sim finished, at least one succeeded, and at least one did not.
- `failed`: Every sim failed.
- `cancelled`: Every sim finished, at least one was cancelled, and none succeeded.

## Types

These are the request and response bodies, from `cascade/models.py`. A field written `X | None` can be `null`. `TraceState`, `SimState` and `RunState` are under States.

### GpuConfig

- `name` (`str`): Accel-Sim tested-cfgs directory name, e.g. "SM90_H100".
- `arch` (`str`): For example, "sm_90".
- `core_clock_mhz` (`float`): First value of -gpgpu_clock_domains in gpgpusim.config.

### KernelLaunch

One kernel launch from the trace's stats_ctx_* file (original hardware).

- `kernel_id` (`int`): Matches kernel-<N> in the trace filename.
- `name` (`str`): Mangled kernel name.
- `grid` (`tuple[int, int, int]`): Grid size, x, y and z.
- `block` (`tuple[int, int, int]`): Block size, x, y and z.
- `instructions` (`int | None`): Instructions the tracer counted. `null` if the kernel's trace was cut short.

### TraceSummary

- `id` (`str`): The profiler's run_name.
- `state` (`TraceState`): Where the trace is in its lifecycle.
- `error` (`str | None`): Why the trace failed. `null` unless `state` is `failed`.
- `created_at` (`datetime`): When the first file of the trace landed.
- `updated_at` (`datetime`): When the app last changed this trace.
- `model` (`str | None`): `metadata.json` `model`, such as `facebook/opt-125m`.
- `layers` (`list[str]`): `metadata.json` `layers`. Empty if missing or not a list.
- `source_gpu` (`str | None`): metadata.json "gpu".
- `trace_gpu_arch` (`str`): metadata.json "trace_gpu_arch", default "sm_90".
- `suggested_sim_config` (`str | None`): `metadata.json` `suggested_sim_config`. The UI preselects it on the New run screen.
- `kernel_count` (`int`): Traced kernels seen so far.
- `bytes` (`int`): Bytes on disk under the trace dir.
- `has_real_timing` (`bool`): True when the trace has real per-kernel timings (`real_timing.json`). The profiler does not write them yet.
- `has_step_timeline` (`bool`): corrected_timeline.json + kernel_mapping.json are in the trace dir.

### TraceDetail

Every field of `TraceSummary`, plus these.

- `metadata` (`dict | None`): The trace's `metadata.json`, parsed. `null` until it arrives.
- `kernels` (`list[KernelLaunch]`): Kernel launches from the trace's `stats_ctx_*` files, by `kernel_id`. Filled in when the trace becomes `ready`.

### RunEntry

- `gpu_config` (`str`): A `GpuConfig.name` whose `arch` matches the trace's `trace_gpu_arch`.
- `count` (`int`): How many sims run this config. Allowed: at least 1, at most 64.

### RunCreate

- `trace_id` (`str`): A trace in state `ready`.
- `entries` (`list[RunEntry]`): One entry per config. Each fans out to `count` sims. Allowed: at least 1 item.

### RunSummary

- `id` (`str`): Generated, `run-` and 12 hex digits.
- `trace_id` (`str`): The trace the run simulates.
- `created_at` (`datetime`): When the run was created.
- `state` (`RunState`): Derived from the sims. See `RunState`.
- `entries` (`list[RunEntry]`): The entries the run was created with.
- `sim_counts` (`dict[SimState, int]`): How many sims are in each state. States with no sims are left out.

### RunDetail

Every field of `RunSummary`, plus these.

- `trace` (`TraceSummary`): The run's trace.
- `sims` (`list[SimSummary]`): Every sim, sorted by `gpu_config` and then `replica`.

### SimSummary

- `id` (`str`): Generated, `sim-` and 12 hex digits. The simulator receives it as `CASCADE_SIM_ID`.
- `run_id` (`str`): The run this sim belongs to.
- `gpu_config` (`str`): The config this sim simulates. The simulator receives it as `CASCADE_GPU_CONFIG`.
- `replica` (`int`): 0-based index within its {gpu_config, count} entry.
- `state` (`SimState`): Where the sim is in its lifecycle.
- `error` (`str | None`): Why the sim failed or went `lost`, from a heartbeat or from the app. A `running` heartbeat clears it.
- `launcher_ref` (`str | None`): Sailbox id or local pid.
- `created_at` (`datetime`): When the run was created.
- `started_at` (`datetime | None`): The first `running` heartbeat.
- `finished_at` (`datetime | None`): When the sim reached a terminal state.
- `last_heartbeat_at` (`datetime | None`): The last heartbeat. `null` before the first one.
- `exit_code` (`int | None`): From the final heartbeat, when the simulator sent one.
- `kernels_done` (`int`): Kernel stats blocks parsed from the log so far.
- `kernels_total` (`int`): The trace's kernel count when the run was created.
- `current_kernel` (`str | None`): The kernel named by the last `launching kernel name:` line in the log.
- `latest` (`SimMetrics`): The most recent totals parsed from the log.
- `log_tail` (`list[str]`): Last 20 lines.

### SimMetrics

- `gpu_tot_sim_cycle` (`float | None`): Simulated cycles so far, over every kernel.
- `gpu_tot_sim_insn` (`float | None`): Simulated instructions so far, over every kernel.
- `gpu_tot_ipc` (`float | None`): Instructions per cycle so far, over every kernel.
- `sim_rate_ips` (`float | None`): gpgpu_simulation_rate, instructions/sec.

### KernelStat

One per-kernel stats block parsed from Accel-Sim output.

- `sim_id` (`str`): The sim that ran this kernel.
- `kernel_index` (`int`): 0-based order of completion within the sim.
- `kernel_name` (`str`): The block's `kernel_name`.
- `kernel_launch_uid` (`int | None`): The block's `kernel_launch_uid`.
- `gpu_sim_cycle` (`int | None`): Cycles this kernel took on the simulated GPU.
- `gpu_sim_insn` (`int | None`): Instructions this kernel ran.
- `gpu_ipc` (`float | None`): This kernel's instructions per cycle.
- `sim_time_ns` (`float | None`): gpu_sim_cycle / core_clock_mhz * 1000.
- `stats` (`dict[str, float | str]`): Every "key = value" line in the block.

### ComparisonRow

- `kernel_index` (`int`): Row position. Kernels are matched by order.
- `kernel_name` (`str`): From real timing if present, otherwise from the first sim that finished this kernel.
- `real_ns` (`float | None`): `duration_ns` from real timing. `null` without real timing.
- `sim_ns` (`dict[str, float | None]`): gpu_config -> median sim_time_ns over replicas.

### Comparison

- `has_real_timing` (`bool`): False until the trace has real timing.
- `configs` (`list[str]`): The run's configs, in entry order, without repeats.
- `rows` (`list[ComparisonRow]`): One row per kernel position.

### SimResults

- `sim` (`SimSummary`): The sim as `SimSummary`.
- `trace_id` (`str`): The trace the sim ran.
- `gpu_config` (`GpuConfig`): The full config. `arch` is `unknown` and the clock is 0 if the config disappeared since the run started.
- `kernels` (`list[KernelStat]`): Every kernel the sim finished, with the full `stats` map.
- `totals` (`SimMetrics`): Same as `sim.latest`.

### RunResults

- `run` (`RunSummary`): The run without its trace and sims, which are below.
- `trace` (`TraceDetail`): The full trace.
- `sims` (`list[SimResults]`): One entry per sim.
- `comparison` (`Comparison`): Same as `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/comparison`.

### SimStepTimeline

- `sim_id` (`str`): The sim that sent it.
- `gpu_config` (`str`): The sim's config.
- `replica` (`int`): The sim's replica.
- `simulated` (`dict`): As sent in `StepTimelineUpload.simulated`.
- `compare` (`dict | None`): As sent in `StepTimelineUpload.compare`.

### SimFile

An output file a sim uploaded with PUT /api/sims/{id}/files/{name}.

- `name` (`str`): Matches FILE_NAME_PATTERN; Accel-Sim's name, plus .gz when the worker gzipped it.
- `size` (`int`): Bytes as stored.
- `content_type` (`str`): From the name: `text/csv` for `.csv`, `text/plain` for `.txt` and `.log`, `application/json` for `.json`, `application/gzip` for `.gz`, and otherwise a guess, falling back to `application/octet-stream`.
- `created_at` (`datetime`): When this version was stored; a re-put replaces the file.

### RunFile

Every field of `SimFile`, plus these.

- `sim_id` (`str`): The sim that uploaded the file.
- `gpu_config` (`str`): The sim's config.
- `replica` (`int`): The sim's replica.

### RunEvent

`RunEvent` is `SnapshotEvent | SimEvent | LogEvent | KernelEvent`. One event on the run event stream. The `type` field says which model it is.

### SnapshotEvent

- `type` (`Literal["snapshot"]`): Always `snapshot`.
- `run` (`RunDetail`): The run as it is at connect time.
- `kernels` (`list[KernelStat]`): Every sim's stats with `stats` emptied; full stats are ~30 KB each.

### SimEvent

- `type` (`Literal["sim"]`): Always `sim`.
- `sim` (`SimSummary`): The sim after a change: state, heartbeat, progress or metrics.

### LogEvent

- `type` (`Literal["log"]`): Always `log`.
- `sim_id` (`str`): The sim the lines came from.
- `lines` (`list[str]`): The new chunk, as the simulator sent it.

### KernelEvent

- `type` (`Literal["kernel"]`): Always `kernel`.
- `stat` (`KernelStat`): A kernel that just finished, with the full `stats` map.
````

The same prompt is at [agent-prompt.md](agent-prompt.md) as plain Markdown, and at [cascade-skill/SKILL.md](cascade-skill/SKILL.md) as a skill with `name` and `description` frontmatter.

## Set up your tool

Each tool below can take the prompt pasted into a chat. To keep it across sessions, save it as a file the tool reads. The commands copy the files from a Cascade checkout. Run them from your project's root, and set `CASCADE` to the checkout's path.

### Claude Code

Save the prompt as a skill. Claude Code loads it when a request matches the skill's description. Use `.claude/skills/` in your project, or `~/.claude/skills/` to have it in every project.

```bash
mkdir -p .claude/skills/cascade
cp "$CASCADE/landing/docs/cascade-skill/SKILL.md" .claude/skills/cascade/SKILL.md
```

To load it in every session instead, append the prompt to your project's `CLAUDE.md`.

```bash
cat "$CASCADE/landing/docs/agent-prompt.md" >> CLAUDE.md
```

### Codex

Codex reads `AGENTS.md` in your project's root, and `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` for every project. Append the prompt to either one.

```bash
cat "$CASCADE/landing/docs/agent-prompt.md" >> AGENTS.md
```

### Cursor

Save the prompt as a project rule in `.cursor/rules/`. This rule has a description, so the agent can pull it in when a request is about Cascade. Cursor's docs list the other ways a rule can apply.

```bash
mkdir -p .cursor/rules
cat > .cursor/rules/cascade.mdc <<'EOF'
---
description: Drive the Cascade app API for traces, runs and simulation results
alwaysApply: false
---

EOF
cat "$CASCADE/landing/docs/agent-prompt.md" >> .cursor/rules/cascade.mdc
```

### Other agents

Paste the prompt at the start of the conversation. If your agent loads skills from `SKILL.md` folders, use [cascade-skill/SKILL.md](cascade-skill/SKILL.md). Otherwise, save [agent-prompt.md](agent-prompt.md) wherever your agent reads project instructions. Check your agent's docs for where that is.

## Docs for agents

These files give an agent the docs without the site around them. The build writes them next to the pages.

- [llms.txt](llms.txt) lists every docs page with a one-line description, in the llms.txt convention.
- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) has every page as Markdown in one file, in the order of the sidebar.
- [agent-prompt.md](agent-prompt.md) is the setup prompt above.
- [cascade-skill/SKILL.md](cascade-skill/SKILL.md) is the setup prompt as a skill.


# Concepts

Page: concepts.html

Cascade has four nouns. A trace is what you captured. A GPU config is what you simulate it on. A run asks for some number of sims per config. A sim is one simulator process working through the trace.

## Trace

A trace is one profiler run: Accel-Sim SASS traces for every kernel the traced layers launched, plus the profiler's `metadata.json`. Its id is the profiler's run name, such as `20261107-120000__facebook_opt-125m__model.decoder.layers.10.self_attn`.

The app keeps each trace as plain files at `$CASCADE_DATA_DIR/s3/cascade/accelsim-traces/<trace id>/`, because `rclone serve s3` writes uploaded objects to disk as files. Sims read the trace from the same path on their own copy of that disk.

A trace records the architecture it was captured on in `trace_gpu_arch`. An H100 trace contains Hopper-only instructions, so it can only run on `sm_90` configs. If `metadata.json` has no `trace_gpu_arch`, the app assumes `sm_90`, which is what the H100 profiler produces.

### Trace states

Diagram: Trace states, from cascade/ingest.py

- `uploading` starts when the first file of the trace appears in the bucket.
- `processing` starts when the upload is complete. [Traces](traces.html#when-an-upload-counts-as-complete) explains how the app decides that.
- `ready` means `traces/kernelslist.g` exists and runs can launch.
- `failed` means `metadata.json` says `status: "failed"`, or post-processing failed.

## GPU config

A GPU config is one of Accel-Sim's tested configs, a directory under `gpu-simulator/gpgpu-sim/configs/tested-cfgs/` such as `SM90_H100`. The app reads two things from each one: the architecture, from the directory name, and the core clock, from the first value of `-gpgpu_clock_domains` in `gpgpusim.config`. The clock turns simulated cycles into simulated time.

## Run

A run is one trace plus a list of entries. Each entry names a config and a count from 1 to 64, so `[{"gpu_config": "SM90_H100", "count": 4}, {"gpu_config": "SM90_H200", "count": 2}]` asks for six sims. The app doesn't store a run's state. It derives the run's state from its sims every time you read it.

| sim states | run state |
|---|---|
| `running`, `succeeded` | `active` |
| `succeeded`, `succeeded` | `succeeded` |
| `succeeded`, `failed` | `partial` |
| `failed`, `failed` | `failed` |
| `cancelled`, `failed` | `cancelled` |
| `cancelled`, `succeeded` | `partial` |
| `cancelled`, `cancelled` | `cancelled` |

## Sim

A sim is one simulator working on one config. Sims of the same entry differ only in `replica`, numbered from 0. Running several replicas of a config tells you whether its numbers are stable.

The app and the sim share ownership of the sim's state. The app moves sims to `launching`, `lost` and `cancelled`, and to `failed` when a launch fails or a sim stays lost too long. Heartbeats from the sim move it to `running`, `succeeded` or `failed`.

### Sim states

Diagram: Sim states, drawn from SIM_TRANSITIONS in cascade/models.py

The diagram is drawn from `SIM_TRANSITIONS` in `cascade/models.py`, which is the only list of allowed moves. Any move outside it is ignored. `failed` and `cancelled` can be reached from every state that hasn't finished, so they are listed under the diagram instead of drawn.

- A sim with no heartbeat for `CASCADE_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_S` seconds, 60 by default, becomes `lost`. The app checks every 5 seconds.
- A `lost` sim that sends another heartbeat goes back to `running`, or straight to `succeeded` or `failed` if that's what it reports.
- A sim that stays `lost` for 10 times the timeout, 600 seconds by default, becomes `failed` with the error `no heartbeat for 600s`, and the app stops its sandbox. Every run finishes eventually.

## How a run launches

When you create a run, the app writes the run and all of its sims as `pending`, returns, and launches in the background. Up to 8 launches run at once.

On Sail (`cascade serve --sims sail`, which the deploy script runs), launching works like this.

1. The app checkpoints its own sandbox once per run, as `cascade-<run id>`. A checkpoint saves the disk, so it includes the ready trace. If a checkpoint with that name already exists, the app reuses it, so a restart mid-launch doesn't take a second one.
2. For each sim, the app starts a new sandbox named `cascade-<sim id>` from that checkpoint with `restore_memory=False`. The fork boots fresh from the saved disk instead of cloning the app's running process.
3. In the fork, the app runs `CASCADE_SIM_CMD` in the background with the sim's environment, and passes the sim id as the call's idempotency key. The command's output goes to `$CASCADE_DATA_DIR/work/sims/<sim id>.out` on the fork's disk.
4. The sim's `launcher_ref` is the fork's sandbox id. When the sim finishes or is cancelled, the app terminates that sandbox.

Every fork of a run starts from the same checkpoint, so every sim reads an identical trace, and the trace is never copied over the network.

Locally (`cascade serve --sims local`, the default), the app runs `CASCADE_SIM_CMD` as a subprocess in its own process group, with the same environment, and `launcher_ref` is the process id. To stop it, the app sends `SIGTERM` to the group and `SIGKILL` after 5 seconds.

> The Sail launcher was written against the Sail SDK 0.17.2 source and is covered by tests with a fake SDK. It hasn't run against the live Sail service yet.

## How sims report back

Sims push and the app listens. A sim needs no public address of its own. It reaches the app at `CASCADE_MAIN_URL` and sends two kinds of request.

- A heartbeat every few seconds, with its state. The reply tells it whether it has been cancelled.
- Its raw output in numbered chunks. The app parses Accel-Sim's per-kernel stats out of the lines itself, so a simulator never has to.

The app stores every chunk, so you can download a sim's full log at any point. It fans every change out to browsers over server-sent events. [Bring your own simulator](simulator.html) has the full contract.


# Deploy the app

Page: deploy.html

`scripts/deploy_sail.py` builds the app's image, starts it in a Sail sandbox, and prints the two URLs you need: the app, and the S3 endpoint the profiler uploads to.

## Before you deploy

- A [Sail](https://docs.sailresearch.com/quickstart) account and API key.
- A Cascade token. Pick any long random string. The UI, the profiler and every sim use it.
- For real simulation, a simulator image: a Docker image with Accel-Sim and its trace post-processor built in. Without one, the app runs the stand-in simulator.

## Deploy with a simulator image

To simulate your traces, pass the simulator image and tell the app where things are inside it.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/atoniolo76/cascade.git
cd cascade
export SAIL_API_KEY=...
export CASCADE_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 24)
uv run --extra sail python scripts/deploy_sail.py \
  --base-image <simulator-image> \
  --sim-cmd "/app/.venv/bin/cascade worker" \
  --accelsim-dir <path to accel-sim in that image>
```

`cascade worker` runs `<accelsim-dir>/gpu-simulator/bin/release/accel-sim.out` on the trace with the sim's config. If the image keeps the post-processor somewhere other than `<accelsim-dir>/util/tracer_nvbit/tracer_tool/traces-processing/post-traces-processing`, add `--postprocess-cmd`. [Bring your own simulator](simulator.html#what-the-image-needs) lists what the image needs.

## Deploy with the stand-in simulator

Leave the three flags out to try the UI and the API first.

```bash
uv run --extra sail python scripts/deploy_sail.py
```

> Without `--base-image`, `--sim-cmd` and `--accelsim-dir`, every sim runs `cascade worker --replay`, which replays a real Accel-Sim run of `facebook/opt-125m` on SM90_H100 (20 vLLM kernels, from `results/20261108-021007-opt125m-h100-accelsim/`). It doesn't simulate your trace, and its numbers are the same for every trace. The image is plain `ubuntu:22.04`, so it has no post-processor. Upload traces that already contain `traces/kernelslist.g`, or they fail in `processing`.

## What the script prints

The script builds the image if needed, creates the sandbox, starts `cascade serve` in it, and waits for the app's port.

```text
creating sailbox 'cascade-main' in app 'cascade' (builds the image if needed)
sailbox:  <sailbox id>
app:      https://<app url>
s3:       https://<s3 url>  (bucket cascade, prefix accelsim-traces, path-style, unsigned)
logs:     /data/cascade-serve.log inside the sailbox
```

| url | use it for |
|---|---|
| app (port 8000) | Open it in a browser and paste your token. The same URL serves the API. |
| s3 (port 9000) | Pass it to the profiler as `--s3-endpoint`. Traces upload here, unsigned and path-style. |

If `CASCADE_TOKEN` isn't set, the script makes one and prints it as `token:`. Save it, because the app accepts nothing else.

## Script flags

| flag | default | what it sets |
|---|---|---|
| `--app` | `cascade` | The Sail app to create the sandbox in. The script creates it if it doesn't exist. |
| `--name` | `cascade-main` | The app sandbox's name. |
| `--base-image` | `ubuntu:22.04` | The Dockerfile's `BASE_IMAGE`, the image the app is layered on. |
| `--sim-cmd` | `cascade worker --replay` on the OPT-125m H100 log | `CASCADE_SIM_CMD`, the command each sim runs. |
| `--accelsim-dir` | `/app/tests/fixtures/accelsim` | `CASCADE_ACCELSIM_DIR`. The default holds real Accel-Sim configs but no simulator. |
| `--postprocess-cmd` | derived from `--accelsim-dir` | `CASCADE_POSTPROCESS_CMD`. |
| `--disk-gib` | Sail's default | The app sandbox's disk limit. Sims fork this disk, so size it for your traces. |

## What's in the image

The `Dockerfile` builds the web UI with Node 22, then layers the app onto `BASE_IMAGE`: rclone 1.76.0, uv with Python 3.12, the app at `/app`, and the Accel-Sim configs and logs from `tests/fixtures`. The app sandbox and every sim fork run this one image. Sail doesn't run the image's `CMD`, so the script starts `cascade serve --sims sail` itself, with your `SAIL_API_KEY`, which the app needs to checkpoint and fork itself.

The sandbox has auto-sleep turned off, so the app keeps running while sims report in.

## Configuration

`cascade serve` reads these environment variables. The table is generated from `cascade/settings.py`.

| variable | default | what it sets |
|---|---|---|
| `CASCADE_TOKEN` | required | The shared bearer token. The UI and every sim send it. The app refuses to start without it unless `CASCADE_NO_AUTH` is set. |
| `CASCADE_NO_AUTH` | false | Local development only. Set to `1` to turn off the token check: the API accepts any request, `/api/health` reports `auth: false`, and the web UI skips its token screen. Never set it on a deployment someone else can reach. |
| `CASCADE_ACCELSIM_DIR` | `/opt/accel-sim-framework` | Accel-Sim checkout. The app reads GPU configs from `gpu-simulator/gpgpu-sim/configs/tested-cfgs/*/gpgpusim.config` under it. |
| `CASCADE_S3_BUCKET` | `cascade` | The bucket the profiler uploads to. It is a directory under `$CASCADE_DATA_DIR/s3/`. |
| `CASCADE_DATA_DIR` | `/data` | Where the app keeps `cascade.db`, the S3 bucket directory `s3/`, sims' output files in `files/`, and scratch files in `work/`. |
| `CASCADE_SIM_CMD` | none | The command each sim runs. On Sail it runs through a shell. Locally it is split into arguments and run without one. Without it, every sim fails at launch. |
| `CASCADE_POSTPROCESS_CMD` | `$CASCADE_ACCELSIM_DIR/util/tracer_nvbit/tracer_tool/traces-processing/post-traces-processing` | Accel-Sim's trace post-processor. The app runs it once per trace as `<cmd> <trace>/traces -j <cpus>`. |
| `CASCADE_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_S` | `60` | Seconds without a heartbeat before a sim becomes `lost`. After 10 times this, a `lost` sim becomes `failed`. |
| `CASCADE_RUN_S3` | `true` | Whether `cascade serve` starts `rclone serve s3` next to the app. Set `false` to run the S3 endpoint yourself. |
| `CASCADE_PUBLIC_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:8000` | The URL sims use to reach the app. Each sim gets it as `CASCADE_MAIN_URL`. |
| `CASCADE_S3_PREFIX` | `accelsim-traces` | The key prefix traces live under. Each trace is `<prefix>/<run_name>/`. |

`cascade serve` takes `--host` (default `0.0.0.0`), `--port` (default 8000), `--s3-port` (default 9000) and `--sims`. `--sims local`, the default, runs each sim as a subprocess of the app. `--sims sail` forks a Sail sandbox per sim.

The S3 endpoint accepts anonymous reads and writes. Anyone with its URL can upload a trace. The app's API and UI need the token.


# Trace a workload

Page: trace-a-workload.html

The profiler, `accelsim_trace.py`, runs a vLLM model on a Modal H100 under Accel-Sim's NVBit tracer and uploads each kernel's trace to your app's S3 endpoint as soon as that kernel finishes.

> Use the streaming profiler from the `validate-accelsim-modal` branch (`accelsim_trace.py` at commit `b348d7d`). The copy at the root of the app branch is an older version that saves to a Modal Volume and has no `--s3-*` flags.

## Set up Modal

The profiler runs on [Modal](https://modal.com). Install the client and log in once.

```bash
pip install modal
modal setup
```

The first run builds an image with NVBit, the tracer and vLLM, which takes a while. Later runs reuse it.

## Pick the layers

Tracing every instruction is slow, so trace one or a few layers, not the whole model. List the layer names first.

```bash
modal run accelsim_trace.py --model facebook/opt-125m --list-layers
```

## Trace and stream

Pass the S3 endpoint that [Deploy the app](deploy.html) printed. The bucket is `cascade` and the endpoint needs path-style addressing.

```bash
modal run accelsim_trace.py \
  --model facebook/opt-125m \
  --layers model.decoder.layers.10.self_attn \
  --prompt "Hello, my name is" \
  --max-tokens 4 \
  --s3-endpoint https://<your-s3-endpoint> \
  --s3-bucket cascade \
  --s3-addressing-style path
```

Before it starts tracing, the profiler checks that the bucket is reachable and stops if it isn't. When it finishes, it prints where the trace went.

```text
Done. Traces at s3://cascade/accelsim-traces/<run name>
```

## What gets uploaded

The tracer writes one `kernel-<N>-ctx_<0x..>.trace.xz` file per kernel and closes it before the next kernel starts. A background thread uploads each closed file and deletes it locally, so the Modal container only ever holds the kernel being traced plus any upload backlog.

After tracing ends, the profiler uploads the rest of the run: the logs, `metadata.json`, `spinlock_detection/spinlock_instructions.txt`, `traces/kernelslist_ctx_*` and `traces/stats_ctx_*`. It goes in sorted path order, so `metadata.json` arrives before the `traces/` files. It uploads them even when tracing failed, so a partial run is as complete as it can be. Everything lands under `s3://cascade/accelsim-traces/<run name>/`.

`metadata.json` holds `model`, `layers`, `prompts`, `max_tokens`, `max_model_len`, `spinlock_handling`, `status` (`ok` or `failed`), `gpu` (from `nvidia-smi`), `accelsim_commit`, and upload counts. It doesn't set `trace_gpu_arch`, so the app uses its default `sm_90`, which is right for an H100.

The profiler doesn't post-process. The app runs Accel-Sim's post-processor once the upload is complete. See [Traces](traces.html).

## Profiler flags

| flag | default | what it sets |
|---|---|---|
| `--model` | `facebook/opt-125m` | The Hugging Face model vLLM loads. |
| `--layers` | `model.decoder.layers.10.self_attn` | Comma-separated module names to trace. |
| `--prompt` | `Hello, my name is` | The one prompt to generate from. |
| `--max-tokens` | 4 | Tokens to generate. Each token is another forward pass to trace. |
| `--max-model-len` | 2048 | vLLM's `max_model_len`. |
| `--run-name` | time, model and layers | The trace's id in Cascade. The default looks like `20261107-120000__facebook_opt-125m__model.decoder.layers.10.self_attn`. |
| `--list-layers` | off | Print layer names and exit without tracing. |
| `--spinlock-handling` | `mark_region` | `mark_region`, `fast_forward` or `none`. Any mode but `none` first runs Accel-Sim's two-pass spinlock detection. |
| `--s3-endpoint` | none | Your app's S3 endpoint. |
| `--s3-bucket` | none, required | Use `cascade`. |
| `--s3-prefix` | `accelsim-traces` | Must match the app's `CASCADE_S3_PREFIX`. |
| `--s3-region` | `auto` | Region name for the S3 client. |
| `--s3-addressing-style` | `auto` | Use `path` for the Cascade endpoint. |

The Modal function has 8 CPUs, 64 GiB of memory and 512 GiB of scratch disk, and times out after 4 hours. Tracing stops after 3.5 hours to leave time for uploads to drain.

## Upload a trace you already have

`scripts/upload_trace.py` uploads a local directory with the same client settings as the profiler and sends `metadata.json` last, with `status` and a `files` list. Use `--meta key=value` to add fields such as `trace_gpu_arch` for a trace from another GPU. Values are strings.

```bash
uv run python scripts/upload_trace.py ./my-run --run-name my-run \
  --endpoint https://<your-s3-endpoint> --meta trace_gpu_arch=sm_80
```

Add `--status failed` to mark the upload as failed. The app then marks the trace `failed` without processing it.


# Traces

Page: traces.html

The app watches its bucket directory. A trace appears on the **Traces** screen as soon as its first file lands, and it's ready once the upload is complete and post-processed.

## Follow a trace

Open **Traces** in the UI, or poll [List traces](api-traces.html#list-traces). Each trace moves through these states.

| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `uploading` | Files are arriving. `kernel_count` and `bytes` grow on each scan, every 2 seconds. |
| `processing` | The upload is complete. The app is running the trace post-processor, unless the upload already has `traces/kernelslist.g`. |
| `ready` | Post-processing produced `traces/kernelslist.g`. Runs can launch. |
| `failed` | `metadata.json` has `status: "failed"`, or post-processing failed. `error` says which. |

Open a trace to see what it came from: the model, the layers, the prompts, the source GPU, the suggested config, and every traced kernel with its grid and block size. The kernel list fills in when the trace becomes `ready`.

## When an upload counts as complete

The app scans `$CASCADE_DATA_DIR/s3/<bucket>/<prefix>/` every 2 seconds. It skips dotfiles, which covers rclone's in-flight `.rclone_temp_put_*` objects. The upload is complete when `metadata.json` exists and one of these holds.

- `metadata.json` has a `files` list, and every listed file is on disk with the listed size in bytes. `scripts/upload_trace.py` writes this list.
- There is no `files` list, every `traces/kernelslist_ctx_*` has a matching `traces/stats_ctx_*`, and the file tree hasn't changed since the previous scan. This is the case for the streaming profiler, which uploads `metadata.json` before its `traces/` files.

If `metadata.json` has `status: "failed"`, the trace goes to `failed` straight away, without processing.

## Post-processing

The profiler uploads raw traces. Accel-Sim reads processed ones, `traces/kernelslist.g` and one `.tracez` per kernel. So the app runs the post-processor once per trace.

```bash
$CASCADE_POSTPROCESS_CMD <trace dir>/traces -j <cpu count>
```

Its output goes to `$CASCADE_DATA_DIR/work/postprocess/<trace id>.log`. If it exits non-zero, the trace fails with the exit code and the last 5 lines of that log. If it succeeds but leaves no `kernelslist.g`, the trace fails too.

An upload that already contains `traces/kernelslist.g` skips post-processing. The quickstart's stand-in trace works this way.

If the app restarts during post-processing, the trace stays `processing` and the post-processor runs again on the next start.

## Where the trace's fields come from

| field | source |
|---|---|
| `id` | The directory name under the prefix, which is the profiler's `--run-name`. |
| `model`, `layers` | `metadata.json`. |
| `source_gpu` | `metadata.json` `gpu`. |
| `trace_gpu_arch` | `metadata.json` `trace_gpu_arch`, or `sm_90` if it's missing. |
| `suggested_sim_config` | `metadata.json` `suggested_sim_config`. The profiler doesn't set it, so the New run screen preselects the first compatible config instead. |
| `kernel_count` | While uploading, the raw `kernel-*.trace` and `.trace.xz` files seen. Once ready, the kernel lines in `kernelslist.g`. |
| `bytes` | Every file under the trace's directory. |
| `kernels` | The rows of `traces/stats_ctx_*`, or `stats.csv` from older tracers. |
| `has_real_timing` | Whether `real_timing.json`, or the file `metadata.json` names in `real_timing`, holds a list of rows with integer `kernel_id`s. |
| `has_step_timeline` | Whether the trace directory holds both `corrected_timeline.json` and `kernel_mapping.json`. The app rechecks on every scan, so it can turn true after the trace is `ready`. See [Step timing](simulator.html#step-timing). |

## Disk space

Traces grow with the layers, tokens and forward passes you trace. A single small layer is tens of MB. Whole models with long prompts reach hundreds of GB. Processed files sit next to the raw ones, so plan for about 2.2 times the uploaded size on the app's disk, and pass `--disk-gib` when you deploy.


# Runs

Page: runs.html

A run simulates one ready trace on a list of GPU configs, with a count for each. Every count is its own sim, and every sim is its own sandbox.

## Launch a run in the UI

1. Open a `ready` trace and choose **New run**.
2. Add a row per config and set its count, from 1 to 64. The trace's `suggested_sim_config` is preselected. Without one, the first compatible config is.
3. Choose **Launch 6 simulations**. The button counts the sims for you. The run screen opens and updates live.

Configs for a different architecture than the trace's `trace_gpu_arch` are disabled. An H100 trace contains Hopper-only instructions, so it runs only on `sm_90` configs such as `SM90_H100` and `SM90_H200`. To model another architecture, trace on that GPU.

## Launch a run over the API

[Create a run](api-runs.html#create-run) takes the trace id and the entries.

```bash
curl -X POST "$CASCADE_URL/api/runs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASCADE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"trace_id": "demo", "entries": [{"gpu_config": "SM90_H100", "count": 4}, {"gpu_config": "SM90_H200", "count": 2}]}'
```

The app checks the request before creating anything.

- The trace must exist (`404`) and be `ready` (`409`).
- Every `gpu_config` must be one [List GPU configs](api-runs.html#list-gpu-configs) returns, with the trace's architecture (`422`).
- `entries` can't be empty and every `count` is 1 to 64 (`422`).

The response is the new run with every sim `pending` or `launching`. Launching happens in the background. [Concepts](concepts.html#how-a-run-launches) walks through it.

## Follow a run

The run screen shows a card per sim with its state, how long since its last heartbeat, kernels done out of the trace's kernel count, the kernel it's on, its latest metrics, and the last lines of its log. Over the API, read [Get a run](api-runs.html#get-run) or subscribe to [Stream run events](api-events.html).

The run's own state comes from its sims.

| sim states | run state |
|---|---|
| `running`, `succeeded` | `active` |
| `succeeded`, `succeeded` | `succeeded` |
| `succeeded`, `failed` | `partial` |
| `failed`, `failed` | `failed` |
| `cancelled`, `failed` | `cancelled` |
| `cancelled`, `succeeded` | `partial` |
| `cancelled`, `cancelled` | `cancelled` |

## Cancel a run

On the run screen, choose **Cancel run** and then **Confirm cancel**, or call [Cancel a run](api-runs.html#cancel-run). Every sim that hasn't finished becomes `cancelled`, the app stops its sandbox, and the simulator's next heartbeat gets `cancel: true`. Sims that already finished keep their results. Cancelling twice is harmless.

## When a sim goes quiet

A sim with no heartbeat for 60 seconds shows as `lost`. It goes back to `running` when it reports again. A sim still `lost` after 600 seconds becomes `failed` and its sandbox is stopped. Both times scale with `CASCADE_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_S`.

## After a restart

The app keeps everything in SQLite at `$CASCADE_DATA_DIR/cascade.db`. When it starts again, it launches any sims still `pending`. Sims on Sail run in their own sandboxes, so they keep going and their heartbeats land again once the app is back.


# Reading results

Page: reading-results.html

Every number Cascade shows comes from Accel-Sim's own output. Sims send raw stdout, and the app parses one stats block per finished kernel out of it.

## Metrics on a sim card

Each sim card shows its latest totals. They update every time the sim sends a log chunk with a new kernel block.

| metric | Accel-Sim line | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Cycles | `gpu_tot_sim_cycle` | Simulated GPU cycles so far, over every finished kernel. |
| IPC | `gpu_tot_ipc` | Instructions per cycle over the whole simulated GPU so far. |
| Sim rate | `gpgpu_simulation_rate` | How fast the simulator itself runs, in simulated instructions per wall-clock second. |
| Kernels | `kernel_name` blocks | Kernel blocks parsed so far, out of the trace's kernel count. |

In the examples on these pages, one sim finished with `gpu_tot_sim_cycle` 76713, `gpu_tot_ipc` 346.2289 and a sim rate of 510774 instructions per second. Those numbers come from the recorded BabelStream log that the stand-in simulator replays.

## Simulated time per kernel

Accel-Sim counts cycles. To turn cycles into time, the app divides by the config's core clock, the first value of `-gpgpu_clock_domains` in its `gpgpusim.config`.

```text
sim_time_ns = gpu_sim_cycle / core_clock_mhz * 1000
```

For example, the first kernel in the captured run took 6174 cycles on `SM86_RTX3070`, whose core clock is 1132 MHz, so its `sim_time_ns` is 6174 / 1132 * 1000 = 5454.06.

## Real against simulated

The comparison panel lines kernels up by position. Row `i` is the `i`th kernel the sims finished, and for each config it shows the median `sim_time_ns` over that config's replicas. With several replicas, one odd sim can't skew the row.

When a trace has real timings from the original GPU, row `i` also shows the `i`th real kernel by `kernel_id`, and the panel shows each config's relative error per kernel and its mean absolute error over all kernels. The app reads them from `real_timing.json` in the trace, or the file `metadata.json` names in `real_timing`, as a list of `{kernel_id, kernel_name, duration_ns, grid, block}`.

> The profiler doesn't capture real timings yet. Until it does, `has_real_timing` is false, `real_ns` is `null` on every row, and the panel shows simulated time only.

## Outputs

A simulator can upload the files it writes. `cascade worker` uploads every file Accel-Sim created or changed in its run directory, such as `kernel-stats.csv`, `gpgpu_inst_stats.txt` and `exit-status.txt`, and then its own log as `accelsim.log.gz`. It does this when the simulator exits, succeeded or failed, before the final heartbeat. A cancelled sim uploads nothing.

The run screen's **Outputs** card groups the files by config, then by replica, with each file's size. Select a sim card, and its panel lists the same sim's files under **Files**. Every file has a download button. A `.csv`, `.txt` or `.log` file up to 16 MiB, gzipped or not, also has a preview button that shows its first 200 lines.

The card has two more buttons. **Perfetto JSON** downloads the run's [Perfetto trace](reading-results.html#the-perfetto-trace). **Open in Perfetto** opens ui.perfetto.dev in a new tab and hands it the same trace, so there is no file to save and open. Both stay disabled until a sim has finished a kernel.

In the examples on these pages, each sim's output files come from a recorded OPT-125m run on `SM90_H100`, which the stand-in copies in with `--replay-outputs`. They don't match the BabelStream log the sim replays.

## The Perfetto trace

The app builds the trace from the kernel stats it parsed, so every run has one, whether or not the simulator wrote its own. It is a Chrome trace JSON file.

- Each config is one process, named `<config> · Accel-Sim simulated GPU`.
- Each replica is one thread in its config's process, named `replica <n> · <sim id>`.
- Each finished kernel is one slice, named `k<uid> <readable name>`, such as `k2 copy_kernel`. The readable name is the one the run screen shows.
- A sim's slices are laid end to end in kernel order. A slice lasts the kernel's `sim_time_ns`, and the time axis is simulated microseconds. A kernel without `sim_time_ns` is left out.
- Each slice's args hold `kernel_name` as recorded, `kernel_index`, `uid`, `gpu_sim_cycle`, `gpu_sim_insn`, `ipc` and `sim_time_ns`. `start_cycle` and `end_cycle` count the sim's cycles before and after the kernel.
- When the trace has real timing, one more process, `Real hardware · <source_gpu>`, holds the measured kernels the same way.

Each slice includes the config's launch latency. Laying kernels end to end leaves out host time, copies and any overlap between kernels.

## Downloads

| download | where | contents |
|---|---|---|
| Run results | **Download results** on the run screen, or [the API](api-runs.html#get-run-results) | One [`RunResults`](types.html#runresults) JSON file: the run, the trace, every sim's per-kernel stats, and the comparison. |
| Sim results | **Results** on a sim card, or [the API](api-runs.html#get-sim-results) | One [`SimResults`](types.html#simresults) file: the sim, its config, its kernels and its totals. |
| Log | **Log** on a sim card, or [the API](api-runs.html#get-sim-log) | The sim's full raw output, as plain text. |
| Output file | The **Outputs** card, **Files** in a sim's panel, or [the API](api-runs.html#get-sim-file) | One file as the sim uploaded it. A `.gz` file stays compressed. |
| Perfetto JSON | **Perfetto JSON** on the **Outputs** card, or [the API](api-runs.html#get-run-perfetto) | The run's simulated kernels as a Chrome trace JSON, named `<run_id>-perfetto.json`. |

Each kernel in a results file has a `stats` map with every `key = value` line in its Accel-Sim block, about 950 keys and 30 KB per kernel. Numbers are parsed as floats, and anything else stays a string. The live run screen leaves `stats` out to stay small. Use the downloads for it.

## How the parser reads a log

A kernel's block starts at a `kernel_name = ...` line and ends at the next `gpgpu_simulation_time`, `launching kernel name:`, `Processing kernel`, `Header info loaded` or `GPGPU-Sim: *** exit detected` line, or at the next `kernel_name`. A block still open when the sim finishes is closed then. The `launching kernel name: X uid: N` line sets the sim's `current_kernel`.

The app stores the raw log as well as the parsed stats. After a restart, it rebuilds a running sim's parser by replaying that sim's stored log, so parsing picks up where it stopped.


# Bring your own simulator

Page: simulator.html

Cascade runs whatever command is in `CASCADE_SIM_CMD` inside each sim. The app ships one, `cascade worker`, which runs Accel-Sim. Any other program that follows this contract can be the simulator: a patched build, or something else entirely.

## The contract

1. Read your identity from the environment.

   | variable | value |
   |---|---|
   | `CASCADE_SIM_ID` | This sim's id, such as `sim-6b4c91e71437`. |
   | `CASCADE_MAIN_URL` | The app's URL, from `CASCADE_PUBLIC_URL`. |
   | `CASCADE_TOKEN` | The bearer token for every request. |
   | `CASCADE_GPU_CONFIG` | The config to simulate, such as `SM90_H100`. |
   | `CASCADE_TRACE_DIR` | The trace's directory. The processed trace is at `$CASCADE_TRACE_DIR/traces/kernelslist.g`. |
   | `CASCADE_ACCELSIM_DIR` | The app's `CASCADE_ACCELSIM_DIR`, where Accel-Sim and its configs live. |

2. Send `POST /api/sims/{id}/heartbeat` with `{"state": "running"}` right away, and again every few seconds. If the reply has `"cancel": true`, stop and exit.

3. Send your output as `POST /api/sims/{id}/logs` with `{"seq": n, "lines": [...]}`, counting `seq` up from 0. Send Accel-Sim's stdout as it is. The app parses the per-kernel stats out of it.
